title: Renewal & EU Sovereignty Activation - BrightLine Systems
next_steps: Priya to run latency and cold-start benchmarks against eu-west-1 private pilot by 2025-09-05
Jordan to send draft amendment with 2x capacity uplift, preferred billing cadence, and pricing sheet by 2025-09-02
Ellen to confirm DPA/SOC2 checklist items and remaining legal questions by 2025-09-09
action_items: Priya Nair | Run benchmark: 10k concurrent tokens/day sim, eu-west-1 private pilot | 2025-09-05
Jordan Reyes | Draft amendment and proposed SOW for retainer uplift (2x) and send pricing table | 2025-09-02
Ellen Kwon | Provide redlines for DPA and confirm required audit LRNs | 2025-09-09

header:
Date: 2025-08-29
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alicia (BrightLine Head of Platform), Samir (SRE), Ellen (Legal), Mateo (CTO)
summary: Check-in focused on renewal year 2: customer is leaning to a retainer uplift (roughly 2x current committed capacity) and wants EU private deployment with data residency. Main open items: latency benchmarks in eu-west-1 private pilot, legal/DPA clarifications, final pricing amendment. Agreed next steps and owners for benchmarks and legal review; SE to run perf test, AE to draft amendment.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call - Jordan from Redwood, Priya our solutions eng, and for BrightLine Alicia, Samir, Ellen and Mateo. How's everybody?
[00:12] Alicia Mora: Hi, yeah all good - thanks.
[00:15] Priya Nair: great, maybe I'll start with a 1 minute recap of where we left off — pilot private VPC spun up in eu-west-1, you were seeing about 35ms median but some tail at 600ms, right Samir?
[00:28] Samir Patel: yeah that's right. The median is good but we've seen spikes during our overnight batch jobs, maybe due to larger seq lengths, and we want to make sure an uplift to retainer doesn't blow our latency SLOs.
[00:40] Jordan Reyes: Exactly. So the goal today is align on renewal uplift numbers, confirm legal items for sovereignty, and Priya to run the targeted benchmarks we discussed.
[00:49] Mateo Ruiz: Quick note from my side — CTO here, thanks. The board wants a clear path to data residency and a hold harmless SLA for regional outages; we need an activation timeline for EU by end of Q4.
[01:02] Jordan Reyes: That's fair. Timeline wise — assuming benchmarks look good and legal signs off on the DPA addendum, we can do a staged rollout: canary week in Sept, then full activation mid-Oct, final by late Nov. That's contingent on capacity and a small infra window.
[01:18] Ellen Kwon: For Legal — we've got three open items: 1) confirm KMS/HSM integration and key escrow options, 2) minimum audit evidence for SOC2 scope, and 3) DPA change re: subprocessors in EU.
[01:32] Priya Nair: On the KMS piece, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; the private deployment can put the control plane behind your VPC and we can route logs to your SIEM. There might be a minor ops step for key rotation.
[01:45] Ellen Kwon: okay, we need the integration doc and who has access — also chain of custody.
[01:50] Priya Nair: I'll attach the KMS integration playbook, though I might spell something wrong in the doc name, it's "kms-integ-guide-v2.pdf" — I'll double check the link.
[01:58] Jordan Reyes: On capacity — Alicia, you mentioned wanting 2x committed tokens compared to current retainer?
[02:05] Alicia Mora: Correct. We're currently at 200M tokens/month committed; leadership is ok moving to 400M for year two provided unit costs don't increase and latency keeps within our SLO.
[02:16] Jordan Reyes: Understood. We can present two pricing options in the amendment: flat uplift with same per-token rate, or tiered pricing where you get volume discounts at 500M+. We'll include both.
[02:28] Mateo Ruiz: Important for us is also burst capacity. Our traffic patterns are spikey — can you guarantee burst up to 2.5x for short windows?
[02:36] Priya Nair: Technical answer: Dedicated pools + burst buckets can get you that, yes. For private (VPC) you'll need reserved capacity on-host with burst credits. There's a short provisioning lead-time for additional GPUs — typically 7-14 days for dedicated add-ons but for private we can pre-stage a node pool.
[02:52] Samir Patel: The provisioning lead-time is what worries us. If we commit to 2x in the contract we need assurance of activation speed.
[02:59] Jordan Reyes: We can include a clause that defines provisioning SLA for burst capacity (e.g., 48-72 hour activation with emergency exception for X hours). I'll work with Rev Ops on that.
[03:10] Ellen Kwon: Also want to flag export controls; some models have restricted components. If you push a quantized variant into EU, need to confirm licensing.
[03:20] Priya Nair: Good point. For curated open models we host, we cross-check licensing; for any proprietary weights we require customer signoff. I'll note an action to validate model variants slated for private pilot.
[03:31] Jordan Reyes: Let's talk benchmarks — Priya?
[03:34] Priya Nair: For the perf test I'll simulate two profiles: 1) interactive low-latency calls (avg 60 tokens, high QPS) and 2) batch long sequences (avg 1,200 tokens) to reproduce overnight spikes. I'll run 10k simulated requests over 24 hours against the eu-west-1 private pilot and capture median/p90/p99 latencies, throughput, and GPU util.
[03:52] Samir Patel: Can you also capture KV-cache hit rates? We've implemented prefix caching in-app and that affects how much GPU is used.
[03:57] Priya Nair: yes — I'll enable KV metrics and include cache hit histograms. One caveat: our telemetry sometimes labels things differently, so names in the dashboard might be slightly off — e.g., "kv_cache_hit_pct" vs "kvHit%" — sorry for noise.
[04:10] Alicia Mora: Also include failover time when we switch to fallback model — that's important for user experience.
[04:14] Priya Nair: noted.
[04:15] Jordan Reyes: For billing we need to confirm whether you prefer monthly or quarterly billing for the uplift. Alicia?
[04:20] Alicia Mora: Quarterly would match our internal procurement calendar. But we might prefer monthly invoicing for burn visibility if possible. Would a quarterly commitment with monthly invoice breakdown be an option?
[04:31] Jordan Reyes: Yes, that's standard — quarterly commit, monthly invoices as a split. We'll put that in the amendment and call out the reconciliation process.
[04:38] Mateo Ruiz: On rollouts — we're keen on an A/B canary. We need Redwood Console access for route-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns so our platform team can monitor during canary.
[04:50] Priya Nair: We'll grant a read-only Console role scoped to your routes for the canary. There may be an extra step to set up SSO.
[04:58] Samir Patel: That brings up SSO — we need SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
[05:02] Jordan Reyes: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Priya will get the SSO metadata and SP details to Ellen for legal and security review.
[05:12] Ellen Kwon: Please include the SP metadata and a short runbook for deprovisioning in case of incident.
[05:18] Priya Nair: I'll attach both. The runbook is titled "sso-scim-runbook-v1.md" in the repo.
[05:23] Jordan Reyes: Anything else on compliance?
[05:25] Ellen Kwon: SOC2 evidences: log retention length, access logs, and encryption at rest/transport. We want to confirm retention windows and whether logs can be routed to our Syslog/Splunk.
[05:36] Priya Nair: Logs can be streamed to your SIEM via TLS; retention window is configurable on the private deployment. We'll include the default values and the change options in the annex.
[05:46] Mateo Ruiz: Great — now about the price point — if you keep the unit price identical at 400M tokens, what's the expected monthly?
[05:55] Jordan Reyes: Rough math: current committed at 200M is $X (we didn't state current in call), so 400M with same unit price doubles the base retainer. There are also uplift charges for private (VPC) — an infra add-on and potential KMS integration fee. I'll show an itemized breakdown in the amendment.
[06:10] Alicia Mora: We need a cap on pass-through infra costs; our finance team cannot accept open-ended cloud egress.
[06:17] Jordan Reyes: Understood — we'll cap pass-through egress and list a not-to-exceed for infra provisioning for the first 12 months.
[06:25] Samir Patel: One operational question — how are software updates handled for private deployments? DBA patches etc.
[06:31] Priya Nair: For private we offer two modes: managed patching (Redwood applies non-disruptive patches during maintenance windows) or self-managed where you apply images. Managed patching is included in the enterprise plan, and we'll map windows per your SRE calendar.
[06:44] Mateo Ruiz: We'll likely go managed, but want full changelog notifications.
[06:48] Priya Nair: Yep — weekly changelog emails and Console release notes.
[06:52] Jordan Reyes: Okay let's summarize next steps and owners — I'll read them out then type into the CRM.
[06:58] Jordan Reyes: Priya to run benchmarks (interactive + batch + KV cache + failover) against eu-west-1 private pilot and share results by 2025-09-05.
[07:08] Priya Nair: confirmed.
[07:09] Jordan Reyes: Jordan to draft contract amendment with 2x committed tokens, burst clause SLA, quarterly commitment with monthly invoicing, and cap on pass-through infra; send by 2025-09-02.
[07:20] Jordan Reyes: Ellen to review DPA and provide redlines by 2025-09-09.
[07:24] Ellen Kwon: yes.
[07:25] Jordan Reyes: Samir to send traffic histograms and tail latency PDFs so Priya can tune the benchmark — due 2025-09-03.
[07:33] Samir Patel: I'll get that to you.
[07:35] Alicia Mora: Also please include a short operational playbook for canary rollback for our on-call team.
[07:41] Priya Nair: I'll include a canary runbook snippet and route-level rollback steps.
[07:45] Jordan Reyes: Anything else?
[07:47] Mateo Ruiz: One small ask — competitive displacement note: GoliathAI offered a cheaper per-token rate but no EU private option in our timeline. Keep an eye on that.
[07:56] Jordan Reyes: Noted. We'll include a positioning note in the amendment.
[07:59] Jordan Reyes: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the KMS doc, SSO metadata, and the draft amendment. Expect a mid-week touchpoint if the benchmarks unearth any regressions.
[08:12] Alicia Mora: Thanks all.
[08:14] Ellen Kwon: thanks.
[08:15] [END]
